attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS forwarder for the shared 10.100.232.0/24 network using Ansible from control node node4. node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.232.11) via a VyOS static-host-mapping and forwards all other queries to the upstream resolver 10.100.232.1. node2 and node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) are configured via a resolvconf head override to resolve through node1. Implementation is a two-play Ansible playbook (/root/ansible-dns/playbook.yml on node4): play 1 uses raw VyOS configure-mode commands (wrapped in sudo bash -c, required because Ubuntu 16.04/VyOS lack a python3 new enough for standard ansible-core 2.21 modules) to set service dns forwarding + static-host-mapping and verifies local resolution; play 2 uses raw SSH commands to install /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/head with nameserver 10.100.232.10, regenerate resolv.conf, and verify both inventory.internal and a public name resolve. Verified idempotent re-runs. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (native reboot), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed DNS forwarding/config persistence and client resolution recovered on every node, including a full successful Ansible playbook re-run from node4 after its own reboot.
